definition: PSI-blast based secondary structure PREDiction (PSIPRED) is a method used to investigate protein structure.
details: It uses artificial neural network machine learning methods in its algorithm. It is a server-side program, featuring a website serving as a front-end interface, which can predict a protein's secondary structure (beta sheets, alpha helixes and coils) from the primary sequence. PSIPRED is available as a web service and as software. The software is distributed as source code, licensed technically as proprietary software. It allows modifying, but enforces freeware provisions by forbidding for-profit distribution of the software and its results.

explainer.lead: PSIPRED predicts a protein's secondary structure from its primary sequence using neural networks, making structural insight available without experimental work.

tiers.eli5: It reads the order of amino acids and guesses which parts will coil into helices and which will lie flat as sheets.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers access it as a web service or as software; a pitfall is its proprietary licence, which forbids for-profit use despite allowing modification.
tiers.paperLevel: It uses artificial neural network methods to assign each residue a label of beta sheet, alpha helix, or coil; like any sequence-based predictor, it cannot guarantee the true global fold.

explainer.example: Submitting a protein sequence to the PSIPRED website returns predicted helices, sheets, and coils along the chain.
